title: Overlapping slots and edge cases
idea: Concurrency for court booking means two overlapping multi-hour requests must never both win; you make check-all-then-write-all one atomic step per court.

analogy.text: Two captains read the same planner at once, see 19:00 empty, and both write their team in. A key to the planner stops that.
analogy.breaks: One key locks the whole planner; the code locks each court separately.

points: Checking free hours, then writing them, is two steps another thread can split.
Bookings span several hours; claiming them one by one can leave half a booking.
A lock per court makes check-and-write atomic without blocking other courts.
Expired holds can be taken over; a late payment for them is refunded.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. P-1 checks whether 18:00 and 19:00 are free.
Before P-1 writes, P-2 checks 19:00 and 20:00. The court is still empty.
Both threads now hold a yes. Each believes 19:00 is free.
P-1 writes both of its hours and reports success.
P-2 acts on its stale yes and overwrites 19:00. Two teams arrive at 19:00.
Safe version. Both threads ask for the lock of court C-1. P-1 gets it.
Holding the lock, P-1 checks and writes both hours as one step.
P-1 unlocks. P-2 takes the lock, checks, and finds 19:00 owned.
P-2 writes nothing and unlocks. One winner, no half-written booking.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier makes both threads look before either writes, so the unsafe race happens on every run. The counts are stable; who wins is not printed.

walk.text: Shared hour owners, one lock per court, a barrier for two threads, and counters.
Two bookings that overlap only at 19:00.
Safe: take the court's lock, then check and write inside it.
Unsafe: check, wait for the other thread, then write regardless.
Join both threads, then report winners, hours claimed and hours stored.

code.title: Holds, late pay, refunds
code.caption: Time is passed in, never read from the system clock, so every run prints the same lines.

walk.text: BK-1 holds 18:00. BK-2 is refused while the hold is live; BK-3 takes over after it expires.
BK-1's payment lands late. Confirm fails, so the money goes back.
The tiered policy refunds less the later a player cancels.
A closure is the ground's fault, so a different policy refunds everything.
A hold is refused only if the hour is paid or the old hold is still live.
Confirm checks the owner and the deadline. Expiry alone is not enough.
Full refund from 24 hours before, half from 4 hours, then nothing.

pitfalls: Do not reserve hour by hour without a lock; a failure leaves half a booking.
Confirm must check the hold still belongs to this booking, not only its time.
Make cancel idempotent; a double click must not refund twice.

quiz.q: What is the first line SlotRace prints?
options: check-then-act: winners=1 hours claimed=2 hours stored=2
check-then-act: winners=2 hours claimed=4 hours stored=3
check-then-act: winners=2 hours claimed=4 hours stored=4
It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier lets both threads see free hours first. Both write two hours, but 19:00 is one map key, so only three are stored.

takeaway: Lock the court, then check and write every hour as one step.

starters: Why not use putIfAbsent for each hour instead of a lock?
